rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Mates repeat themselves. Whoever recognizes the pattern does not need to calculate everything.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: The first is the back-rank mate: the black king is trapped behind its own pawns.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: The 8th rank has no defense. Look for the piece that can reach it.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Give checkmate with the rook, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! Back-rank mate: the pawns trap their own king.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The rook goes up to d8 and checks along the 8th rank. The king has nowhere to go.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.d1d7.1: The rook reaches the 7th rank, but gives no check.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.d1d7.2: Let's go back: the check comes along the king's rank.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: That move is not mate. Let's go back: look at the black king's rank.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Give checkmate with the rook, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: That is why players open a window for the king by advancing a pawn in front of it.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: Remember the pattern: king trapped behind its pawns and a check along the back rank.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: The second is the supported queen: she checks right next to the king, protected by another piece.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: The bishop on d3 aims at the pawn on h7. So does the queen on h5.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Give checkmate with the queen, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! Checkmate: the king cannot capture the queen, who is protected.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The queen captures on h7, right next to the king. The bishop protects her.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.h5f7.1: The queen captures on f7, but nobody protects her there.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.h5f7.3: Let's go back: the queen needs a piece to protect her.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move is not mate. Let's go back: look at the square the bishop aims at.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Give checkmate with the queen, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: The king cannot run either: the black rook and pawns take its squares.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Remember the pattern: queen next to the king and protected. It is one of the most common mates.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Now I will show two more patterns: the smothered mate and the Arabian mate.
rot.demos.sufocado.e1: The smothered mate: the king is surrounded by its own pieces, with no free square.
rot.demos.sufocado.l1: The knight jumps to f7 and gives check.
rot.demos.sufocado.l2: A knight's check cannot be blocked, and the king has no square: checkmate.
rot.demos.arabe.e1: The Arabian mate: rook and knight together. The knight protects the rook and watches an escape.
rot.demos.arabe.l1: The rook goes to h7 and checks, right next to the king.
rot.demos.arabe.l2: The knight protects the rook and covers g8, the escape square. The rook covers g7: checkmate.
rot.demos.arabe.l3: Now it's your turn: recognize the pattern and give mate.
rot.pratica.sufocado.enunciado: The black king is surrounded by its own pieces. Give checkmate with the knight.
rot.pratica.sufocado.fim: Well done. Smothered mate: a knight's check cannot be blocked.
rot.pratica.arabe.enunciado: Rook and knight together. Give checkmate with the rook.
rot.pratica.arabe.fim: Perfect. Arabian mate: the rook gives check, the knight holds the rest.
rot.pratica.arabe.err.a7a8: That is check, but the king escapes to g7. Bring the rook next to the king. Try again.
rot.pratica.corredor.enunciado: The black rook defends the 8th rank. But if it is captured, who defends? Give mate.
rot.pratica.corredor.fim: That's it! The rook captures the defender, and the back-rank mate is done.
